Sanctions are negative diplomatic actions that impose a penalty on the target Civilization and decrease their [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_RELATIONSHIP_TOOLTIP]Relationship[/TIP].
Espionage missions are secret diplomatic actions that only decrease [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_RELATIONSHIP_TOOLTIP]Relationship[/TIP] with the target Civilization if revealed.

Diplomatic Projects are diplomatic actions that can be taken with [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_INDEPENDENT_POWER_TOOLTIP]Independent Power[/TIP] or [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_SUZERAIN_TOOLTIP]Suzerained[/TIP] [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_CITY_STATE_TOOLTIP]City-States[/TIP].

Each point of War Support a Civilization has over its opponent's War Support reduces that Opponent's Unit [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_COMBAT_STRENGTH_TOOLTIP]Combat Strength[/TIP] and [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_SETTLEMENT_TOOLTIP]Settlement[/TIP] [icon:YIELD_HAPPINESS][b]Happiness[/b].[NN]More War Support can be gained by spending [icon:YIELD_DIPLOMACY][b]Influence[/b].

Experience is gained by [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_COMMANDER_TOOLTIP]Commander[/TIP] as units engage in combat within their [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_COMMAND_RADIUS_TOOLTIP]Command Radius[/TIP].[NN]When a Commander gains enough Experience, they receive a [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_PROMOTION_TOOLTIP]Promotion[/TIP].

All Towns have the Growing Town Focus, enabling [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_GROWTH_RATE_TOOLTIP]Growth[/TIP].[NN]Once per [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_AGE_TOOLTIP]Age[/TIP], Towns with at least 7 [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_POPULATION_TOOLTIP]Population[/TIP] may choose a second Town Focus. This grants a powerful effect to the Town while active.[NN]In addition, while that Town Focus is active, the Town distributes its [icon:YIELD_FOOD][b]Food[/b] to all [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_CONNECTED_TOOLTIP]Connected[/TIP] [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_CITIES_TOOLTIP]Cities[/TIP] instead of growing.

Connected Settlements are those that have a direct connection to each other by land or water.[NN]Land connections require a road directly linking both [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_SETTLEMENT_TOOLTIP]Settlements[/TIP]. Merchants can build roads to make direct connections to Settlements that are within [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_TRADE_RANGE_TOOLTIP]Trade Range[/TIP] of each other.[NN]Water connections require both Settlements to be on the same [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_CONTINENT_TOOLTIP]Continent[/TIP] and either have a [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_CITIES_TOOLTIP]City[/TIP] center adjacent to Coast or a Water [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_BUILDINGS_TOOLTIP]Building[/TIP].

Command Radius is the number of tiles around a [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_COMMANDER_TOOLTIP]Commander[/TIP] that gain benefits from their [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_PROMOTION_TOOLTIP]Promotions[/TIP] and [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_COMMENDATION_TOOLTIP]Commendations[/TIP].

Promotions are bonuses that a [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_COMMANDER_TOOLTIP]Commander[/TIP] can gain through [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_COMMANDER_EXPERIENCE_TOOLTIP]Experience[/TIP].[NN]Reaching the final Promotion in a tree unlocks a [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_COMMENDATION_TOOLTIP]Commendation[/TIP].

Commendations are extremely powerful bonuses that a [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_COMMANDER_TOOLTIP]Commander[/TIP] can choose each time they reach the final [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_PROMOTION_TOOLTIP]Promotion[/TIP] in a tree.

Trade Routes are established by sending a Merchant to a foreign [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_SETTLEMENT_TOOLTIP]Settlement[/TIP] within [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_TRADE_RANGE_TOOLTIP]Trade Range[/TIP].[NN]You receive a copy of every [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_RESOURCES_TOOLTIP]Resource[/TIP] from that Settlement, while the foreign Settlement gains increased [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_TRADE_INCOME_TOOLTIP]Trade Income[/TIP].

Trade Range is the maximum distance [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_TRADE_ROUTE_TOOLTIP]Trade Routes[/TIP] can extend from [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_SETTLEMENT_TOOLTIP]Settlements[/TIP] in your [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_TRADE_NETWORK_TOOLTIP]Trade Network[/TIP].[NN]There are two types of Trade Range, Land and Sea, depending on whether the route crosses land or water.

Your Trade Network includes all [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_SETTLEMENT_TOOLTIP]Settlements[/TIP] that are within [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_TRADE_RANGE_TOOLTIP]Trade Range[/TIP] of another Settlement that is already in your Trade Network, starting from your [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_CAPITAL_TOOLTIP]Capital[/TIP].[NN][TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_RESOURCES_TOOLTIP]Resources[/TIP] from any Settlement within the Trade Network can be assigned to any other Settlement within the Trade Network.

Trade Income increases a [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_SETTLEMENT_TOOLTIP]Settlement[/TIP]’s [icon:YIELD_GOLD][b]Gold[/b] yield for each [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_TRADE_ROUTE_TOOLTIP]Trade Route[/TIP] established there by another Civilization.[NN]The more Improved [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_RESOURCES_TOOLTIP]Resources[/TIP] a Settlement has, the greater its Trade Income per route.

Independent Powers have a single home Village and do not expand.[NN]They can be either Friendly or Hostile. Settling too close to, or attacking, a Friendly Independent Power will make them Hostile.[NN]Through Diplomacy, you can befriend Independent Powers and eventually become their [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_SUZERAIN_TOOLTIP]Suzerain[/TIP].
Ageless effects persist unchanged across all [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_AGE_TOOLTIP]Ages[/TIP].
Continents are contiguous areas of the world that can include islands.[NN]Use the Continents Lens to see continental boundaries.

A Bridge allows [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_LAND_UNITS_TOOLTIP]Land Units[/TIP] to move over a [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_NAVIGABLE_RIVER_TOOLTIP]Navigable River[/TIP] without having to [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_EMBARK_TOOLTIP]Embark[/TIP].[NN]They are cheaper to build where a Road has already formed a Ferry across the River.

Walls [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_FORTIFIED_DISTRICTS_TOOLTIP]Fortify Districts[/TIP].[NN]Walls must be built on the [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_CITIES_TOOLTIP]City[/TIP] Center or adjacent to another [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_DISTRICT_TOOLTIP]District[/TIP] with Walls.[NN]They can only be purchased on the City Center.

Zone of Control applies to tiles adjacent to a unit that exerts a Zone of Control.[NN]Entering a unit's Zone of Control ends movement, but attacks can still be made.[NN]Ranged, Support and [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_SIEGE_UNITS_TOOLTIP]Siege Units[/TIP] do not exert a Zone of Control.
Units are Stationed in a [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_SETTLEMENT_TOOLTIP]Settlement[/TIP] when located in one of its [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_DISTRICT_TOOLTIP]Districts[/TIP].
Units are Garrisoned in a [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_SETTLEMENT_TOOLTIP]Settlement[/TIP] when located in one of its [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_FORTIFIED_DISTRICTS_TOOLTIP]Fortified Districts[/TIP].
Units that start their turn on a Burning tile take damage.

Commanders are a special type of [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_SUPPORT_UNIT_TOOLTIP]Support Unit[/TIP] that can gain [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_COMMANDER_EXPERIENCE_TOOLTIP]Experience[/TIP] and can assemble other units of the same domain to form an Army, Fleet, or Air Squadron, allowing them to move together with their Commander.[NN]Assembled Units are vulnerable and cannot attack until the units have been deployed onto tiles adjacent to the Commander.[NN]Defeated Commanders will respawn in your [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_CAPITAL_TOOLTIP]Capital[/TIP] after a delay.

Treaties are a type of diplomatic action with ongoing effects that can increase or decrease [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_RELATIONSHIP_TOOLTIP]Relationship[/TIP] and cannot be Supported, only Accepted or Rejected.
Units with Stealth are not visible to enemies greater than 1 tile away.

Infected [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_SETTLEMENT_TOOLTIP]Settlements[/TIP] suffer from [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_UNREST_TOOLTIP]Unrest[/TIP], stop [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_GROWTH_RATE_TOOLTIP]growth[/TIP] and spread Infection to [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_CONNECTED_TOOLTIP]Connected[/TIP] Settlements.[NN]Units that start their turn on Infected tiles take damage.

Support Units cannot initiate attacks, but they can be attacked by [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_MILITARY_UNIT_TOOLTIP]Military Units[/TIP].[NN]Support Units are allowed to occupy the same tile as Military Units.
Civilian Units cannot attack or be attacked.[NN]They can freely enter other Civilizations’ territory and share tiles with any Unit.
Military Units can both attack and be attacked by other Units.

[TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_SETTLEMENT_TOOLTIP]Settlements[/TIP] suffering from Unrest cannot purchase Units, [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_BUILDINGS_TOOLTIP]Buildings[/TIP], [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_IMPROVEMENT_TOOLTIP]Improvements[/TIP], or Repairs. [NN]They incur a [icon:YIELD_HAPPINESS][b]Happiness[/b] penalty until the Unrest ends.

Leaders with a Helpful [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_RELATIONSHIP_TOOLTIP]Relationship[/TIP] can form an Alliance and must keep a positive Relationship to maintain it.[NN]Allies will be called to join each other's Wars.

Relics are [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_GREAT_WORKS_TOOLTIP]Great Works[/TIP] that increase [icon:YIELD_CULTURE][b]Culture[/b] and [icon:YIELD_HAPPINESS][b]Happiness[/b] in the [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_SETTLEMENT_TOOLTIP]Settlements[/TIP] where they are slotted.

Religions are established in the [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_EXPLORATION_AGE_TOOLTIP]Exploration Age[/TIP].[NN]Missionaries convert [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_SETTLEMENT_TOOLTIP]Settlements[/TIP] by spreading Religion on [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_DISTRICT_TOOLTIP]Districts[/TIP] and [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_IMPROVEMENT_TOOLTIP]Improvements[/TIP]. Settlements that have both a District and an Improvement converted to the same Religion are considered to be following that Religion.[NN]Religious Beliefs determine what benefits are gained from converting Settlements to follow a Religion.
Units with the Skirmish ability gain +50% [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_COMBAT_STRENGTH_TOOLTIP]Combat Strength[/TIP] from [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_FLANKING_TOOLTIP]Flanking[/TIP].

Units with the Pirate ability can cross borders of other Civilizations, Plunder [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_TRADE_ROUTE_TOOLTIP]Trade Routes[/TIP] between non-Allied Civilizations, and attack Units of non-Allied Civilizations without going to War.

Units with the Amphibious ability do not suffer a [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_COMBAT_STRENGTH_TOOLTIP]Combat Strength[/TIP] penalty when [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_EMBARK_TOOLTIP]Embarked[/TIP] and do not end their movement when [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_EMBARKED_TOOLTIP]Embarking[/TIP] or Disembarking.

Artifacts are [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_GREAT_WORKS_TOOLTIP]Great Works[/TIP] that increase [icon:YIELD_CULTURE] [b]Culture[/b] in the [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_SETTLEMENT_TOOLTIP]Settlements[/TIP] where they are slotted.
A Natural Wonder is a special map feature, such as The Grand Canyon or Great Barrier Reef. They provide unique bonuses and increased yields.

Tourism is the score used for the [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_CULTURAL_VICTORY_TOOLTIP]Cultural Victory[/TIP]. It is a measure of how culturally dominant your empire is and comes from sources such as [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_WONDERS_TOOLTIP]Wonders[/TIP], [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_NATURAL_WONDER_TOOLTIP]Natural Wonders[/TIP], [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_UNIQUE_IMPROVEMENT_TOOLTIP]Unique Improvements[/TIP], [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_CELEBRATIONS_TOOLTIP]Celebrations[/TIP], [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_RELIC_TOOLTIP]Relics[/TIP], and more.
One of four Victory types. A Military Victory is awarded when a leader reaches military dominance over all other players. This is measured by Dominion.
One of four Victory types. A Cultural Victory is awarded when a leader reaches cultural dominance over all other players. This is measured by [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_TOURISTS_TOOLTIP]Tourism[/TIP].
One of four Victory types. A Scientific Victory is awarded when a leader reaches 100 Innovation while having an active Launch Pad.
One of four Victory types. An Economic Victory is awarded when a leader reaches economic dominance over all other players. This is measured by [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_GDP_TOOLTIP]GDP[/TIP].
The first of three Ages of the game.
The second of three Ages of the game.
The third of three Ages of the game.
Unique Units are special Units, usually associated with a single Civilization. They often have unique bonuses and effects and are typically stronger than their generic counterpart.

The Age in which a Civilization is at its strongest. During a Civilization's Apex Age, it may have access to [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_UNIQUE_UNITS_TOOLTIP]Unique Units[/TIP], [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_UNIQUE_BUILDING_TOOLTIP]Unique Buildings[/TIP], and [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_UNIQUE_IMPROVEMENT_TOOLTIP]Unique Improvements[/TIP]. It also has a special [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_CIVIC_TOOLTIP]Civic Tree[/TIP] where additional bonuses can be unlocked.

An [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_AGE_TOOLTIP]Age[/TIP] in which a Civilization is not in its [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_APEX_AGE_TOOLTIP]Apex Age[/TIP]. Time-Tested Civilizations have access to a limited set of [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_CIVIC_TOOLTIP]Civics[/TIP] and may study [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_SYNCRETISM_TOOLTIP]Syncretism[/TIP] to unlock the ability to adopt the ways of Civilizations in their Apex Age.

Dominion is the score used for the [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_MILITARY_VICTORY_TOOLTIP]Military Victory[/TIP]. It is a measure of how militarily dominant your empire is and comes primarimly from [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_SETTLEMENT_TOOLTIP]Settlements[/TIP] you found and conquer.

The Capital [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_CITIES_TOOLTIP]City[/TIP] of an Empire. The first City founded automatically becomes the Original Capital. At the start of each [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_AGE_TOOLTIP]Age[/TIP], each Empire has the opportunity to change their Capital.

Innovation represents your progress in the [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_SCIENTIFIC_VICTORY_TOOLTIP]Scientific Victory[/TIP]. You earn Innovations many ways, including assigning [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_CODEX_TOOLTIP]Codices[/TIP], researching [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_MASTERY_TOOLTIP]Tech Masteries[/TIP], and completing [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_SCIENCE_PROJECT_TOOLTIP]Scientific Projects[/TIP]. Once you reach 100 Innovations and have a Launch Pad, you'll trigger the Scientific Victory countdown.

GDP represents your progress in the [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_ECONOMIC_VICTORY_TOOLTIP]Economic Victory[/TIP]. You earn GDP each turn after Researching The Wheel for each [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_RESOURCES_TOOLTIP]Resource[/TIP] assigned to [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_CITIES_TOOLTIP]Cities[/TIP], each [icon:YIELD_GOLD][b]Gold[/b] [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_BUILDINGS_TOOLTIP]Building[/TIP] constructed after Researching Currency, and more. Once you've reached sufficient dominance against all other players, you'll trigger the Economic Victory countdown.

Rural tiles are tiles with [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_IMPROVEMENT_TOOLTIP]Improvements[/TIP]. They provide Rural [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_POPULATION_TOOLTIP]Population[/TIP] and will follow your Rural [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_RELIGION_TOOLTIP]Religion[/TIP]. If a [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_BUILDINGS_TOOLTIP]Building[/TIP] is constructed on top of a Rural Tile, it becomes an Urban tile.

Your Government determines the bonus your Empire receives during a [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_CELEBRATIONS_TOOLTIP]Celebration[/TIP]. Early each [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_AGE_TOOLTIP]Age[/TIP], you'll be asked to select your Government.

War Weariness occurs when you're at War and your [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_WAR_SUPPORT_TOOLTIP]War Support[/TIP] is below the War Support of your opponent. War Weariness causes reduced [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_COMBAT_STRENGTH_TOOLTIP]Combat Strength[/TIP] for all units as well as [icon:YIELD_HAPPINESS][b]Happiness[/b] penalties across all [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_SETTLEMENT_TOOLTIP]Settlements[/TIP]. Captured Settlements, especially those captured from someone you’re at war with, suffer increased [icon:YIELD_HAPPINESS][b]Happiness[/b] penalties.

Triumphs are optional challenges you can complete in an [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_AGE_TOOLTIP]Age[/TIP]. Each Triumph is themed after one of the game’s six [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_ATTRIBUTE_TOOLTIP]Attributes[/TIP]: Cultural, Scientific, Military, Diplomatic, Expansionist, and Economic. Completed Triumphs provide [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_DEDICATION_TOOLTIP]Dedications[/TIP] or instant bonuses.
Triumph Sets determine the list of Triumphs active in your campaign.
Your Treasury is the amount of [icon:YIELD_GOLD][b]Gold[/b] you have available to spend. Each turn the amount in your Treasury grows or shrinks by your [icon:YIELD_GOLD][b]Gold[/b] yield.

Each [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_SETTLEMENT_TOOLTIP]Settlement[/TIP] has a Population count that Grows based on the amount of [icon:YIELD_FOOD][b]Food[/b] the Settlement produces. When a new Population is gained, you can assign that Population to an unimproved tile to place an [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_IMPROVEMENT_TOOLTIP]Improvement[/TIP] or on an Urban tile to place a [icon:SPECIALIST][TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_SPECIALIST_TOOLTIP]Specialist[/TIP], once unlocked.

Every leader has a Relationship level with all other leaders: Hostile, Unfriendly, Neutral, Friendly, or Helpful. These Relationships determine how likely the other leaders will accept or support your [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_ENDEAVOR_TOOLTIP]Endeavors[/TIP], what the penalty is for declaring a [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_SURPRISE_WAR_TOOLTIP]Surprise War[/TIP], and how likely they are to declare war on you.
A Surprise War occurs when a leader declares War against a non-Hostile leader. Surprise Wars have heavy [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_WAR_SUPPORT_TOOLTIP]War Support[/TIP] penalties.
A Formal War occurs when a leader declares War against a Hostile leader. Formal Wars do not have a [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_WAR_SUPPORT_TOOLTIP]War Support[/TIP] penalty.
Minor Triumphs are Triumphs that reward instant bonuses.
Major Triumphs are Triumphs that reward [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_DEDICATION_TOOLTIP]Dedications[/TIP].

In order to capture a [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_SETTLEMENT_TOOLTIP]Settlement[/TIP], you must destroy any Defensive Fortifications of the Settlement and have a [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_MILITARY_UNIT_TOOLTIP]Military Unit[/TIP] occupy those tiles. Defensive Fortifications take extra damage from [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_SIEGE_UNITS_TOOLTIP]Siege Units[/TIP].

Masteries are optional nodes on the [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_TECH_TOOLTIP]Tech[/TIP] and [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_CIVIC_TOOLTIP]Civic Trees[/TIP]. They often provide unique bonuses or other unlocks related to the main Tech or Civic.
Another name for the [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_SCIENTIFIC_VICTORY_TOOLTIP]Scientific Victory[/TIP].
Scientific Projects are [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_CITIES_TOOLTIP]City[/TIP] Projects that provide [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_INNOVATION_TOOLTIP]Innovation[/TIP].

You have four Advisors, one for each Victory Type. The Advisors provide suggestions, advice, and warnings to help you complete their associated victory. You can follow an Advisor to get additional advice as the game progresses.

Syncretism allows your empire to incorporate the [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_UNIQUE_UNITS_TOOLTIP]Unique Units[/TIP] or infrastructure of other Empires while playing a [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_TIME_TESTED_TOOLTIP]Time-Tested[/TIP] Civilization or gain a powerful [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_TRADITION_TOOLTIP]Tradition[/TIP] to further enhance into your Civilization.
At the start of each [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_AGE_TOOLTIP]Age[/TIP], you can select up to three Dedications among those you've unlocked to provide a powerful bonus to your Empire for the entire Age.
Merchants allow your empire to initiate Trade Routes with other Civilizations and City-States, yielding the Resources of the Settlement the Merchant trades with, as well as a sum of Gold.

Studying Technologies furthers your Civilization's understanding of the world around you. Mastering a Technology, or studying its Mastery, grants bonus effects related to the corresponding Technology base Node.
A Holy City is a [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_SETTLEMENT_TOOLTIP]Settlement[/TIP] a [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_RELIGION_TOOLTIP]Religion[/TIP] was founded in.

The Palace is a [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_BUILDINGS_TOOLTIP]Building[/TIP] in the center of a leader's [icon:NOTIFICATION_SELECT_CAPITAL] [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_CAPITAL_TOOLTIP]Capital[/TIP]. When a Capital is conquered or changed, the Palace moves to the new Capital, and the previous Settlement's Palace becomes a City Hall.

Rivers are sources of fresh water and ideal spots for [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_SETTLEMENT_TOOLTIP]Settlements[/TIP]. There are two types of Rivers: [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_MINOR_RIVER_TOOLTIP]Minor Rivers[/TIP] and [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_NAVIGABLE_RIVER_TOOLTIP]Navigable Rivers[/TIP].

Natural Disasters are environmental effects on the map that can damage Units or [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_PILLAGED_TILE_TOOLTIP]Pillage[/TIP] [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_BUILDINGS_TOOLTIP]Buildings[/TIP] and [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_IMPROVEMENT_TOOLTIP]Improvements[/TIP].
Blizzards are a kind of [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_NATURAL_DISASTERS_TOOLTIP]Natural Disaster[/TIP] where snow falls from the sky.
Duststorms are a kind of [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_NATURAL_DISASTERS_TOOLTIP]Natural Disaster[/TIP] where dust is kicked up.
Floods are a kind of [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_NATURAL_DISASTERS_TOOLTIP]Natural Disaster[/TIP] where Rivers overflow.
Hurricanes are a kind of [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_NATURAL_DISASTERS_TOOLTIP]Natural Disaster[/TIP] where tropical storms worsen.
Tornadoes are a kind of [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_NATURAL_DISASTERS_TOOLTIP]Natural Disaster[/TIP] where air currents form a column touching the ground.
Thunderstorms are a kind of [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_NATURAL_DISASTERS_TOOLTIP]Natural Disaster[/TIP] where lightning illuminates the sky.
Volcanic Eruptions are a kind of [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_NATURAL_DISASTERS_TOOLTIP]Natural Disaster[/TIP] that affects tiles around Volcanoes.
Pillaged [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_BUILDINGS_TOOLTIP]Buildings[/TIP] and [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_IMPROVEMENT_TOOLTIP]Improvements[/TIP] do not grant their yields and effects until they are Repaired.
Fallout is a kind of [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_NATURAL_DISASTERS_TOOLTIP]Natural Disaster[/TIP] that comes from Nuclear weaponry.
Walls can be damaged, leading them to lose their effects when the District Health drops to 0.

Occupation is when enemy Units reside in opposing [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_FORTIFIED_DISTRICTS_TOOLTIP]Fortified Districts[/TIP]. In Wars, all Fortified Districts must be occupied by a Unit in order to capture the Settlement.
